clue.text: Second class bank for liquidation?

parts.note: B is the grade label for second class, after A
a bank is an institution that lends, a lender

explanation.surface: A query about a second-rate bank heading for winding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidation' suggests a failing bank being wound up, but here it means turning food to liquid in a kitchen machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance purees solids into liquid, so it is a device for liquidation in the cooking sense.

clue.text: Halve a little over 28 part one

indicators.note: the word for a little goes over, covering, the other piece

parts.note: a bit is a little
the first part of 28 across is dry, and sec means dry, of wine

explanation.surface: Split something just over twenty-eight into the first section.
explanation.walkthrough: '28 part one' points at the first word of the answer to 28 across, which in wine terms is the French sec; 'over' means covering, so one piece goes around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something into two equal parts is to halve it.

clue.text: Drunken seamen forced to clean the bottom

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering, so the letters of seamen are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sailors who got drunk are made to scrub the ship's lower deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a past tense but describes the liquid treatments themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: These are liquids injected into the rectum to flush the bowel, so they are forced in to clean the bottom.

clue.text: Result of having falsely named one "fat" and "round"

definitions.text: Result of having falsely named one "fat" and "round"

indicators.note: falsely tells us the letters are set out wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Calling someone fat and round untruthfully has consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges NAMED, I, FAT and O; and the whole clue describes slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander or libel, damaging a reputation with false claims, is what comes from falsely calling someone fat.

clue.text: Sculptor takes perch home

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod
in means at home

explanation.surface: An artist chisels a fish and carries it back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' suggests the fish; it is the old unit of length, also called a rod or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Draws force to give self backing

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, a fighting force

indicators.note: backing tells us the word self is read from its end to its start
this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lotteries persuade people to fund their own support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for prize lotteries; 'to give backing' turns the self piece round.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffles are prize draws in which tickets are drawn at random, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: One's relations can be tedious

parts.note: relations here are tales recounted, not relatives; a skilled storyteller's anecdotes may drag

explanation.surface: Family members can be boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family, but means accounts or stories told.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tells anecdotes well is a storyteller, and their stories are relations.

clue.text: Rage at what goes into the atmosphere

definitions.meaning: smoke or gas given off into the air

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to seethe angrily and a gas or vapour emitted into the air.

clue.text: A lighter version of lead compound

indicators.note: a version is a different form, so the letters of a lighter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lighter type of a lead-based chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' clashes with 'lead' as a heavy metal, nudging toward weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is lead monoxide, a yellow compound used in glass and ceramics.

clue.text: Lad finds opening in Devon

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name, a typical lad
a mouth is an opening

explanation.surface: A young man discovers a gap in the county of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the answer is a seaside town there at the mouth of the River Sid.
explanation.definitionFit: The resort town lies on the Devon coast, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: Does woman have odd life on this?

definitions.text: Does woman have odd life on this?

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: the odd letters, first and third, of the word life are taken

explanation.surface: A question whether a single woman leads a strange life when left unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' picks L and F from life. A woman 'on the shelf' is an old idiom for one thought past marrying age.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of being left on the ledge describes a woman supposedly too old to marry, so the clue asks about that place.

clue.text: Wed at start of last month with 10% off

indicators.note: tells us the month piece and its companion stand at the head of the word for wed

parts.note: December, DEC, is the final month of the year
this is clue 10, and ten per cent of ten is one, the Roman numeral I
to wed is to marry, here mated

explanation.surface: Someone got married at the start of December after taking a pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: '10%' leans on the clue's own number: a tenth of 10 is 1, Roman I. Decimation originally meant killing one soldier in ten, so the answer fits 'off' in the slang sense of killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for killing them, and the old meaning of the answer is killed one in ten.

clue.text: Industry claiming no reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of claiming no are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade that resists any change to its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracting coal from pits is a heavy industry, long central to the British economy.

clue.text: In the Algarve by a long way round

parts.note: far means by a great distance or degree
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A traveller in southern Portugal goes on a long detour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coastal region; its capital and airport city is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the regional capital of Portugal's southern coast, so it lies within that region.

clue.text: Fruit of sin in the Spanish race?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: tells us the word for sin sits inside the race

parts.note: the Derby is a famous English horse race
to err is to sin or go wrong

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Spanish horse race bears sinful fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is run at Epsom; 'in' sets the sin inside the race, after the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: These small dark berries of the elder tree are a fruit used for wine and cordial.

clue.text: Hit land? My goodness!

parts.note: to strike is to hit
to alight is to come down and land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Strike the ground hard? Well, fancy that!
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This dated British exclamation expresses surprise, just like the mild oath in the clue.

clue.text: Brain addled with cryptic clue having no solution

indicators.note: addled means muddled, so the letters of brain are scrambled together with those of clue
cryptic means puzzling, a second sign that the clue word is mixed up too

explanation.surface: A confused mind faced with a puzzling clue cannot crack it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addled' and 'cryptic' both signal the jumbling of BRAIN and CLUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease beyond remedy cannot be fixed, so like an unsolvable problem it has no solution.

clue.text: Wrestles furiously and gets very hot

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild motion, so the letters of wrestles are churned

explanation.surface: A grappler fights hard and ends up sweating.
explanation.definitionFit: To be oppressively hot and sweaty is to become very hot.

clue.text: Tom starts in sport with Manx cat, an unusual creature

indicators.note: tells us that letter goes inside the word for sport

parts.note: to play is to sport

indicators.note: the word Tom gives its starting letter
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a word for a cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat starts playing with a tailless Isle of Man cat, an odd animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives T, put 'in' PLAY; 'Manx' docks PUSS to PUS, as the Manx breed has no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed egg-laying mammal of Australia is famously strange, an unusual creature.

clue.text: Lose courage when disciplined — it's laid down

parts.note: to wilt is to droop and lose nerve
to be on the carpet is to be summoned for a telling-off by the boss

explanation.surface: Someone loses their nerve when being reprimanded, while a rule is laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilton is a Wiltshire town famous for woven floor coverings; 'on the carpet' means being reprimanded.
explanation.definitionFit: This woven floor covering is something fitted flat on a floor, so it is laid down.

clue.text: Town in New York with a Cayuga Lake view

definitions.text: Town in New York with a Cayuga Lake view

indicators.note: the answer is in view within the words with a Cayuga

explanation.surface: A New York town looks out over Cayuga Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'with a Cayuga'; the town, home of Cornell University, sits at the lake's southern end.
explanation.definitionFit: This upstate New York city lies at the head of Cayuga Lake, overlooking it.

clue.text: With leader stepping down it indeed gets corrected

indicators.note: the first letter moves down one place in the word

parts.note: read as it in deed: the word it placed in deed

explanation.surface: Once the boss resigns the text really does get fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it indeed' is read as IT in DEED, giving DEITED; 'With leader stepping down' moves its D one place down.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been revised and put right by an editor has been corrected.

clue.text: Much the greater part of what was nicked is returned

indicators.note: returned tells us the shortened word is written back to front
most of the word is kept, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: nicked is British slang for stolen

explanation.surface: Most of the stolen goods are given back to their owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the greater part of' drops EN from STOLEN to leave STOL; 'is returned' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural word for a great quantity, as in plenty of something, means much.

clue.text: Spoken, not aloud

parts.note: say the phrase not aloud and it comes out like not allowed, meaning forbidden

explanation.surface: Words that were said, though quietly, under the breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems self-contradictory; the trick is that 'not aloud', spoken, is identical in speech to 'not allowed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not allowed is forbidden, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Collect — there's nothing difficult about it

indicators.note: the word for difficult goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Gathering things up is easy, nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HARD around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass and store things away is to collect them.

clue.text: Press turns up for seaweed

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: The press decides to cover the seaweed story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses IRON in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese edible red algae dried into sheets for sushi is a seaweed.

clue.text: Bush perhaps began in excessive optimism

definitions.text: Bush perhaps began in excessive optimism

indicators.note: tells us the letter is set inside the word for excessive optimism

parts.note: euphoria is an intense, often unwarranted feeling of happiness

indicators.note: the word Bush began with its first letter

explanation.surface: Perhaps President Bush started out in a state of overconfidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'began' gives B, the first letter of Bush, which 'in' puts inside EUPHORIA. The answer is a genus of spurges, many of them shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurge genus includes many shrubby plants, so a bush is one example of it.

clue.text: Cook of a sort

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters of a sort are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is a chef of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges A SORT; and the whole clue defines it, since roasting is one kind of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is one particular way of cooking in an oven, so it is a cook of a sort.

clue.text: One is sent to Reform Chapel

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A member is dispatched to join a Nonconformist place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Reform' rearranges I, IS and SENT. 'Reform' and 'Chapel' suggest Protestant worship; the answer is the papal chapel in the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican's famous chapel with Michelangelo's ceiling carries this name, so it stands for Chapel by association.

clue.text: Firm ground for the US in the twenties

definitions.meaning: land that is solid and not waterlogged or sea

definitions.text: for the US in the twenties
definitions.meaning: under Prohibition in the 1920s America banned alcohol, so it was teetotal territory

explanation.definitionFit: Solid earth is ground that is not wet, and Prohibition America was a country without alcohol.
